open-question.question: The headless-chain decision lands the page edit only after a confirming run of the new fable-high sweep settings on this repository, but the inline sweep exists only once this milestone's tasks are complete, by which time this milestone's own questions are already answered. Which run counts as the confirming run, and does the documentation task wait within this milestone for a later milestone's first sweep or land on some other confirmation?
open-question.alternative: The page edit is the last task of this milestone and lands inside it. The first inline sweep of the next milestone, run at fable high, counts as the confirming run. If that run falls short, the fix is a revert-then-correct in the milestone that ran it. Milestone 30 already worked this way: its headless-chain task landed within milestone 30 once both skills existed, and the values were checked afterwards against the next milestone's first review pass. This follows the one precedent the run-before-record rule already has. The milestone finishes with its goal fully delivered, documentation and host trees included, and the check still happens on a real sweep over real questions, not on a stand-in. The page names fable high for the sweep before any run has confirmed it. That reverses the plain reading of the recorded decision, which says the edit lands only after a confirming run, so the headless-chain decision's wording would have to be read or revised as landing first and confirming afterwards. Any mismatch is found only after users of the page may have copied the new lines.

Once the inline sweep skill and its host rebuild are complete, the confirming run is made inside this milestone on a scratch branch or worktree. That tree puts back this milestone's own recommended but unrecorded state, for example the tree just before the recent `Recommendation-answer:` commits, carrying the new skill. The sweep then runs there at `--model "fable" --effort high`. The scratch branch is thrown away, and the documentation task, ordered after the skill task, lands once the run matches the committed answers. The run happens before the page records the settings, just as the decision says. It uses real questions from this repository that already have known recorded outcomes to compare against, and nothing waits on a later milestone. It needs a fixture setup the workflow has never used: rebuilding a past document state with a future skill, running a headless sweep against it, and throwing away the commits it makes. It also tests only the few recommendation-bearing questions this milestone had, which may never exercise cascades or contradictions. And the task list gains a manual, non-reproducible step that the completion procedure has to run and verify.

alternative.id: Defer page edit to next milestone

open-question.alternative: This milestone leaves the four answer-sweep lines as they are, at `opus`. That stays runnable, because an inline skill runs on either model. The page edit moves out of scope, and the milestone records that the edit lands in the next milestone once that milestone's first inline sweep has run at fable high. It follows the rule as written. Nothing is recorded before a real run confirms it, the confirming run is a real sweep over new questions, and this milestone needs no fixture work. This milestone's goal lists headless chains among the surfaces it updates, so the goal's scope would have to shrink. The next milestone also inherits a documentation chore that has nothing to do with its own goal, and the page keeps recommending opus for a skill whose cost profile no longer suits it until that milestone gets to it.

No separate run of the sweep is needed. The inline recommendation pass has already run at fable high on this repository, including this milestone's own recommendation annotation. The headless-chain decision says the inline sweep has the same run shape as that line, so that run is taken as the confirmation. The page edit lands with this milestone's other documentation tasks. Nothing waits and no fixture is built. The decision's own argument, that the inline sweep pays for the whole-set context once per run just like the recommend line, is exactly what an earlier run at those settings has already shown works. It confirms a different skill by analogy, not the sweep itself. The sequential folds, cascades, per-answer commits, and the `requirements.md` that keeps growing across one long run are not what a single recommendation pass does, so the run-before-record rule is met in name only. It also sets a precedent that weakens the rule for later settings changes.
open-question.recommendation: Milestone 30's rule as recorded confirms the values against the next milestone's first run of the new skills, and its headless-chain task landed inside milestone 30 exactly that way, so the same reading keeps this milestone's goal whole and confirms on a real sweep over new questions; the recorded decision's after-a-confirming-run wording is read as that precedent. Replay builds a fixture the workflow has never used for a handful of questions, Defer shrinks the goal and hands the next milestone a chore, and the recommend-line run confirms a different skill by analogy.
